title: Autoimmune Bullous Disease — Treatment Ladder
subtitle: By disease and phase of therapy: induction → maintenance → adjunct/refractory

induction.text: Rituximab 1 g IV × 2 (D0 + D14) ★ — first-line per PEMPHIX trial
induction.detail:
Rituximab (anti-CD20) 1 g IV on D0 and D14 is first-line per PEMPHIX RCT (Joly 2017, PMID 28342637): superior complete remission at 24 months vs prednisone alone (89% vs 34%), lower cumulative steroid dose, fewer adverse events.

Alternative / combination: Prednisone 1–1.5 mg/kg/day if rituximab unavailable or contraindicated; taper once disease controlled. Initiate steroid-sparing agent (azathioprine or MMF) early if prednisone used. PDAI score guides response assessment.

maintenance.text: Rituximab re-dose at clinical relapse; taper and discontinue prednisone; continue azathioprine or MMF
maintenance.detail:
After rituximab induction: monitor PDAI and anti-Dsg3/Dsg1 ELISA every 3–6 months. Redose rituximab at first sign of relapse (rising titer + new lesions) — fixed redosing schedules (e.g., 500 mg at month 12) are emerging.

If prednisone-based: taper by 10–20% every 4 weeks once PDAI falls below 15; target complete remission off all therapy (CRoff). Steroid-sparing: azathioprine 1–3 mg/kg/day or MMF 2–3 g/day.

adjunct.text: Refractory: IVIG 2 g/kg/cycle; immunoadsorption (if available); cyclophosphamide; dapirolizumab pegol (investigational)
adjunct.detail: Refractory PV (incomplete response to rituximab + steroid): IVIG 2 g/kg/cycle as adjunct can accelerate clinical remission. Immunoadsorption (IA) rapidly reduces anti-Dsg titers; often used peri-rituximab in severe disease (European centers). Cyclophosphamide IV pulse or oral for life-threatening disease. Emerging: efgartigimod (FcRn blocker), dapirolizumab, IgG4 bispecific antibody approaches. PMID: 31498102.

induction.text: Prednisone 0.5–1 mg/kg/day (lower dose than PV — no mucosal disease); rituximab if moderate–severe
induction.detail: PF without mucosal involvement generally responds to lower-dose systemic steroids than PV. Prednisone 0.5–1 mg/kg/day initiated with early steroid-sparing agent. Rituximab 1 g ×2 is effective for moderate–severe PF and recommended for refractory disease. Dapsone 50–150 mg may control limited superficial PF. Anti-Dsg1 ELISA guides response.

maintenance.text: Taper prednisone; MMF 2–3 g/day or azathioprine as steroid-sparing; dapsone for limited stable disease
maintenance.detail: Steroid taper similar to PV. MMF (mycophenolate mofetil) 2–3 g/day is preferred steroid-sparing agent in many centers. Dapsone 50–150 mg can maintain remission in limited superficial PF. Monitor anti-Dsg1 titers; rising titer + new lesions indicates relapse. Fogo selvagem endemic variant may require long-term low-dose maintenance.

adjunct.text: Rituximab if not already used; hydroxychloroquine for mild refractory; IVIG as adjunct in severe
adjunct.detail: Refractory PF (rare): rituximab 1 g ×2 as per PV protocol. Hydroxychloroquine 200–400 mg/day may have steroid-sparing benefit in limited disease. IVIG 2 g/kg/cycle for severe refractory. Sun protection essential (UV can trigger PF flares — especially fogo selvagem). PMID: 31498102.

induction.text: Superpotent topical clobetasol propionate 0.05% BID ★ — preferred for most patients
induction.detail:
Topical clobetasol propionate 0.05% applied BID to entire body surface (except face) is the preferred induction therapy per Joly 2002 RCT (PMID 11821508): non-inferior to oral prednisone 1 mg/kg for disease control; significantly lower 1-year mortality (41% vs 58% in elderly with extensive disease).

Mild–moderate BP alternative: Doxycycline 200 mg/day + niacinamide 1.5 g/day — reasonable for frail elderly with contraindications to superpotent topical steroids or systemic steroids.

Oral prednisone 0.5 mg/kg/day: used when topical therapy is impractical (extensive disease, patient unable to apply). BPDAI guides severity staging. PMID: 35743598.

maintenance.text: Taper topical clobetasol over 12 months; add MMF or methotrexate for extensive or relapsing disease
maintenance.detail:
Taper schedule: after initial 4-week induction at full dose, reduce clobetasol frequency and area over 12 months. Anti-BP180 ELISA titer guides tapering — rising titer predicts relapse.

MMF 2–3 g/day or methotrexate 5–15 mg/week as steroid-sparing adjuncts for extensive BP or patients requiring prolonged topical steroids (skin atrophy, adrenal suppression risk). Doxycycline 100–200 mg/day as maintenance for patients who responded to doxycycline induction. PMID: 35743598.

adjunct.text: Refractory: omalizumab (anti-IgE); dupilumab (anti-IL-4/13); rituximab; oral prednisone ± azathioprine
adjunct.detail: BP is a Th2/IgE-mediated disorder — targeted biologics are increasingly used for refractory disease. Omalizumab (anti-IgE, 300 mg SC q4 weeks): case series and retrospective data show efficacy for steroid-refractory BP, particularly in patients with elevated total IgE. Dupilumab (anti-IL-4Rα): growing evidence from case series for eosinophilic, pruritic BP refractory to standard therapy. Rituximab: effective in refractory BP (smaller evidence base than for pemphigus). DPP-4 inhibitor-triggered BP: discontinue offending drug — may achieve remission without immunosuppression. PMID: 35743598.

induction.text: Stratify by severity: dapsone (mild oral) → prednisone + dapsone (moderate) → cyclophosphamide + prednisone (severe ocular/laryngeal)
induction.detail:
Mild (oral only, no scarring): Dapsone 50–150 mg/day (check G6PD first) ± topical steroid on oral mucosa.

Moderate (multiple sites, non-ocular): Prednisone 1 mg/kg/day + dapsone or MMF.

Severe (ocular, laryngeal, esophageal): Cyclophosphamide 1–2 mg/kg/day PO or IV pulse (2 g/m²) + prednisone 1 mg/kg/day. High-dose IV cyclophosphamide rapidly stabilizes ocular scarring.

URGENT ophthalmology: all patients with ocular MMP require ophthalmologist co-management for conjunctival biopsy, DIF, symblepharon monitoring. PMID: 35743598.

maintenance.text: Long-term steroid-sparing immunosuppression; ophthalmology and ENT co-management; monitor for new mucosal sites
maintenance.detail:
After cyclophosphamide induction (ocular severe): switch to MMF 2–3 g/day or azathioprine once remission achieved. Duration of treatment: often years; MMP tends to be chronic and slowly progressive.

Monitor: periodic slit-lamp exam (ophthalmology) for conjunctival scarring progression. Nasal endoscopy (ENT) if nasopharyngeal involvement. Esophageal involvement: periodic dilation if dysphagia + stricture. Dental involvement: specialist dental care to prevent tooth loss. PMID: 35743598.

adjunct.text: Rituximab for refractory; surgical management of established cicatrization; anti-laminin 332 → malignancy screen
adjunct.detail:
Rituximab 1 g ×2 or 375 mg/m² ×4 (lymphoma protocol): effective for cyclophosphamide-refractory MMP; growing evidence from case series and small trials. IVIG 2 g/kg/cycle as adjunct in severe refractory cases.

Surgical interventions: Lysis of conjunctival symblepharon (ophtho), tarsorrhaphy for corneal protection, esophageal dilation, laryngeal dilation, urethral dilation as needed for cicatricial sequelae — always with concurrent immunosuppression to prevent post-procedural flare.

Anti-laminin 332 MMP: malignancy screen (colonoscopy, gynecologic exam, CT) at diagnosis and annually for 2 years. PMID: 35743598.

induction.text: Dapsone 50–200 mg/day ★ — rapid response within 72 h; strict gluten-free diet (GFD)
induction.detail:
Dapsone: Start 25–50 mg/day, titrate to 50–200 mg/day. Dramatic symptomatic relief within 24–72 h is almost pathognomonic for DH (response supports diagnosis). Dapsone does not treat the underlying celiac enteropathy — GFD is required for that.

Pre-dapsone mandatory checks: G6PD enzyme level (hemolytic anemia risk), baseline CBC and reticulocyte count, LFTs. Monitor CBC at 2 weeks (dose-dependent methemoglobinemia, Heinz body hemolytic anemia) and every 3 months thereafter.

Gluten-free diet (GFD): Strict lifelong GFD is the definitive treatment — treats both the enteropathy and the skin disease. PMID: 35743598.

maintenance.text: Continue dapsone + GFD; expect dose reduction over months–years as GFD takes effect; target dapsone discontinuation if on strict GFD
maintenance.detail:
As strict GFD is maintained, anti-eTG/tTG IgA titers fall, intestinal mucosa normalizes (over months), and dapsone requirements decrease. Many patients can discontinue dapsone after 2–5 years of strict GFD.

Monitor: anti-tTG IgA at 6 and 12 months to confirm dietary compliance. DH patients on GFD have normalized small bowel histology and celiac cancer risk. Dietitian referral for GFD education is essential. BSACI/BSG guidance: also monitor bone density (DXA) — celiac enteropathy causes malabsorption. PMID: 35743598.

adjunct.text: Sulfapyridine 500–2000 mg/day if dapsone intolerant; sulfamethoxypyridazine (colchicine rarely used); nutritional supplementation
adjunct.detail:
Sulfapyridine 500–2000 mg/day: alternative if dapsone not tolerated (G6PD deficiency, severe anemia, agranulocytosis, dapsone hypersensitivity syndrome). Less effective than dapsone but well-tolerated. Adequate fluid intake to prevent crystalluria.

Sulfamethoxypyridazine (not available in all countries): another alternative.

Nutritional supplements: Iron, folate, vitamin B12, vitamin D, calcium — supplement for malabsorption from celiac enteropathy. Monitor bone density (DXA).

Oats: Controversy — uncontaminated oats tolerated by most DH/celiac patients but avoid initially. PMID: 35743598.
